text:
If you apply for an IPO with $10 and get allotted, you’ll pay the IPO price plus a 0.5% broker fee and a 0.1% SEBI transaction fee. The stock then trades at the market price; if you hold it, you’ll face the usual capital‑gain tax (0% long‑term if >1 yr, 15–20% short‑term if <1 yr). For Reliance on Zerodha (delivery), the round‑trip cost on a ₹10,000 position is about ₹38.15 (0.38% of the value) – that includes STT, SEBI, exchange, stamp duty and DP. After that, any gain is taxed at 20% short‑term if you sell within a year. If you want to keep the stake longer, the tax drops to 12.5% once you cross the ₹1.25 lakh exemption threshold.

Regarding NVDA: buying $10 worth of fractional shares on a zero‑commission broker will give you about 0.046 shares. At the current 25.2% CAGR, that $10 would grow to roughly $12.50 in one year. To hit the 10× target would need several years of high‑CAGR compounding—roughly 4 years at a 63.6% decade CAGR. For a faster play you might look at near‑term movers like RGC or APPN, but the odds are slim and the risk high.

If you’re interested in cars or battery makers, we can flag top Indian names like Maruti (MARUTI.NS), Tata Motors (TATAMOTORS.NS) or battery firms such as Amara Raja (AMARAJANA.NS) and Apollo (APOLLOHOSP.NS).
